title: French Toast
description: Skillet French toast made with thick bread, a cinnamon-vanilla egg custard, and a gently browned buttery finish for breakfast or brunch.
ingredients: Maple syrup and berries, for serving
instructions: Leave the bread uncovered briefly so its surface is dry enough to take up custard without breaking down.
Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, sugar, and salt in a shallow dish until the egg is fully dispersed.
Heat a wide skillet or griddle over medium-low heat; the aim is to set the custard before the bread becomes too dark.
Melt a little butter and coat the cooking surface.
Soak two slices at a time, turning once, until the custard has reached the middle without saturating the bread.
Lift each slice and allow excess custard to fall back into the dish.
Cook until the first side is golden and the edges look set.
Turn and brown the second side, lowering the heat if the butter begins to darken too quickly.
Continue with the remaining bread, adding butter as needed and holding finished slices warm only briefly.
Serve hot with maple syrup, fruit, or a light dusting of cinnamon or icing sugar.
tips: Thick, slightly stale bread holds its shape better than soft fresh slices.
Moderate heat gives the egg mixture time to cook through.
Whisk the custard again between batches because cinnamon settles quickly.
commonMistakes: Thin, fresh bread can collapse if it stays in the custard too long.
High heat can brown the surface before the egg custard has set.
An overcrowded pan makes turning the slices difficult.
substitutions: Texas toast is a sturdy alternative to brioche or challah.
Replace part of the milk with half-and-half for a richer custard.
Dairy-free milk and plant-based butter can be used if needed.
storage: Refrigerate fully cooled slices for up to three days.
Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven to restore a crisp edge.
Freeze portions between parchment for up to two months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Cinnamon French Toast
description: Cinnamon French toast with thick bread, a lightly sweetened vanilla custard, and a golden butter-cooked exterior.
ingredients: 8 thick slices brioche or Texas toast
instructions: Lay the bread out briefly so the outer surface dries and can take the custard without becoming weak.
Whisk the eggs and milk until the mixture is uniform.
Add cinnamon, vanilla, brown sugar, and salt, whisking until the sugar is mostly dispersed.
Warm a wide skillet over medium-low heat and coat it lightly with butter.
Dip each slice, turn it once, and let both sides take on the cinnamon custard.
Hold the slice over the dish for a moment so extra custard does not collect in the pan.
Cook in batches until the first surface is deeply golden.
Turn and cook until the second side is browned and the middle feels softly set.
Use fresh butter between batches and stir the custard before each new slice to redistribute the cinnamon.
Serve hot with maple syrup and more cinnamon if desired.
tips: Mix the custard again before each batch so cinnamon does not settle.
Thick bread gives the middle time to become custardy without falling apart.
Medium-low heat helps both the bread and egg mixture cook evenly.
commonMistakes: An excessive amount of cinnamon can form dry clumps on the surface.
Soft bread becomes fragile when soaked for too long.
Burnt butter leaves bitter dark marks on the toast.
substitutions: Challah is a suitable alternative to brioche.
Light brown sugar or granulated sugar both work in the custard.
A small pinch of nutmeg adds another warm spice note.
storage: Refrigerate cooked slices for up to three days.
Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven.
Freeze cooled cooked slices for up to two months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Burritos
description: Pan-crisped breakfast burritos filled with softly scrambled eggs, ham, melting cheese, and tomato for a hearty portable breakfast.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack or mozzarella
instructions: Warm the tortillas briefly so they bend easily without splitting.
Whisk eggs with sour cream, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and add the egg mixture.
Draw the eggs gently into soft curds, taking them off the heat while they still look moist.
Arrange tortillas flat and portion the eggs across the lower third of each one.
Add ham, cheese, and tomato, leaving enough empty tortilla at the sides and edge for a secure roll.
Fold the sides inward, then roll from the bottom into a compact burrito.
Warm a thin coating of oil in a clean skillet and put the burritos in seam-side down.
Turn until the exterior is crisp and golden and the cheese has melted inside.
Let the burritos rest briefly before slicing or wrapping for later.
tips: Keep the eggs a little soft because they finish cooking during the crisping stage.
A moderate amount of filling makes rolling far easier.
Beginning seam-side down helps close the wrap.
commonMistakes: Cold tortillas are more likely to tear as they are rolled.
Wet fillings can soften the tortilla quickly.
Eggs cooked until dry may become rubbery after reheating.
substitutions: Cooked bacon or breakfast sausage can replace ham.
Cheddar works in place of Monterey Jack.
Leave out tomato when preparing burritos for freezing.
storage: Refrigerate wrapped burritos for up to three days.
Freeze individual burritos for up to one month.
Reheat until the centre is steaming hot.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Casserole
description: An oven-baked breakfast casserole of hash browns, bacon, softened vegetables, eggs, and cheddar, cut into warm shareable squares.
ingredients: 2 cups frozen diced hash browns, thawed
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and coat a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with butter.
Soften the onion and bell pepper in a skillet, cooking off visible moisture before they go into the dish.
Spread the thawed hash browns across the prepared dish.
Distribute the vegetables and bacon evenly over the potatoes.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth and slightly aerated.
Pour the egg mixture slowly so it settles around the filling rather than sitting in one corner.
Scatter cheddar over the top in an even layer.
Bake until the edges are puffed and the middle no longer appears liquid.
Rest for about 10 minutes so the eggs firm enough for neat portions.
Cut into squares and serve warm with hot sauce or fresh herbs if wanted.
tips: Thawing the potatoes avoids excess moisture in the base.
Cook watery vegetables before assembling the dish.
Take the casserole out once the centre is set to keep the eggs tender.
commonMistakes: Wet, frozen potatoes can make the casserole watery.
Overbaking gives eggs a rubbery texture.
Slicing immediately produces untidy portions.
substitutions: Cooked sausage can replace bacon.
Monterey Jack works instead of cheddar.
Use spinach only after wilting and squeezing it dry.
storage: Refrigerate covered leftovers for up to four days.
Reheat individual pieces gently.
Freeze cooled portions for up to two months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Sausage Breakfast Casserole
description: An overnight sausage breakfast bake with bread, egg custard, and cheddar, cooked until the centre is set and the top is golden.
instructions: Cut the bread into cubes and spread them through a greased 9-by-13-inch dish.
Scatter browned, crumbled sausage evenly over the bread.
Whisk eggs, milk, and salt together, then pour the custard across the bread and sausage.
Cover the surface with shredded cheddar.
Cover and chill overnight so the bread can absorb the egg mixture.
Bake uncovered at 350°F until the centre is set and the top is golden.
tips: Brown the sausage first and drain any excessive fat.
An overnight rest gives the bread time to take up the custard.
Check the centre for doneness instead of relying solely on the clock.
commonMistakes: Skipping the rest can leave dry bread pieces in the finished bake.
Unbrowned sausage can release extra fat and moisture into the dish.
Removing the casserole before the middle is set leaves the egg undercooked.
substitutions: A mild or sharp cheddar both work in this bake.
Use sturdy sandwich bread, brioche, or another bread you enjoy.
A similarly sized oven-safe dish can replace the 9-by-13-inch pan.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly before refrigerating.
Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to three days.
Reheat portions until hot throughout.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Eggs Benedict
description: Eggs Benedict assembled from toasted English muffins, warmed Canadian bacon, softly poached eggs, and a lemony butter hollandaise.
instructions: Toast the muffin halves until golden and keep them warm while the other parts are prepared.
Warm the Canadian bacon in a skillet until lightly browned, then put a slice on each muffin half.
Bring a wide pan of water to a quiet simmer and add vinegar; a hard boil can break up the whites.
Crack each egg into a small cup, ease it into the water, and poach until the white is set around a soft yolk.
Blend egg yolks and lemon juice until smooth.
With the blender on low, stream in the warm melted butter slowly until the sauce becomes thick and glossy.
Season with salt and cayenne, loosening with a little warm water only if the sauce is too thick.
Lift the eggs with a slotted spoon and blot the underside briefly.
Place one egg over each bacon-topped muffin and spoon the warm hollandaise over it.
Finish with chives and serve without delay.
tips: Keep poaching water at a quiet simmer.
Add butter slowly so the hollandaise stays emulsified.
Have the muffins and bacon ready before poaching eggs.
commonMistakes: Rapidly boiling water can tear delicate whites.
Butter added too quickly can split hollandaise.
A finished Benedict cools quickly if it sits before serving.
substitutions: Ham or crisp bacon can replace Canadian bacon.
Toasted sourdough rounds can replace English muffins.
Add spinach for a Florentine-style variation.
storage: Poached eggs are at their best immediately.
Refrigerate leftover cooked components separately for up to two days.
Make hollandaise fresh for the most reliable texture.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Hash Browns
description: Skillet hash browns made from well-dried russet potato shreds, cooked in a thin layer for a crackly crust and a soft potato middle.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil or bacon fat
instructions: Scrub or peel the potatoes, then shred them with the coarse side of a box grater.
Pile the shreds into a clean tea towel and twist hard over the sink until the towel is no longer releasing much liquid.
Loosen the potato strands in a bowl and distribute the onion powder through them without compressing the mixture.
Warm a heavy 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add half of the oil and butter and wait until the butter stops foaming vigorously.
Scatter in half of the potatoes and gently level them into a loose, thin round; leave them alone rather than pressing repeatedly.
Let the underside brown for 5 to 6 minutes, adjusting the heat down if the butter darkens before the potatoes colour.
Season the exposed side, then turn the round with a broad spatula, or turn it in manageable wedges if that is easier.
Drizzle the remaining cooking fat around the edge and brown the second side until it feels firm and crisp.
Move the finished hash browns to a warm plate or rack, then cook the second batch in the same way.
Add a final pinch of seasoning and bring them to the table immediately.
tips: Dry potato shreds thoroughly before they meet the pan; surface water prevents browning.
A heavy pan holds its heat better when the cold potatoes are added.
Cook in two thin rounds instead of making one thick layer.
commonMistakes: Leaving water in the shreds gives the potatoes a steamed, pale finish.
Moving the potatoes before a crust forms makes the round difficult to turn.
Using high heat throughout can scorch the butter while the centre remains undercooked.
substitutions: Rendered bacon fat can replace the olive oil for a savoury, smoky note.
For a mild onion flavour, fold in a little grated onion after squeezing it dry.
Ghee is a useful alternative to butter when a slightly higher cooking temperature is needed.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and keep them covered in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
Restore the crust in a dry skillet, oven, or air fryer rather than microwaving.
Freeze fully cooled portions in a single layer, then transfer them to a freezer-safe container for up to 1 month.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Home Fries
description: Golden breakfast potato cubes tossed with tender onion, red pepper, smoked paprika, and parsley, with browned sides and a soft centre.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
instructions: Put the potato cubes in a saucepan, cover with lightly salted water, and bring them just to a low boil.
Cook until a knife meets only slight resistance at the outside of a cube, about 5 to 6 minutes, then drain them completely.
Leave the potatoes in the colander for a few minutes so residual steam dries their surfaces.
Heat a broad, heavy skillet over medium-high heat and coat the base with avocado oil.
Tip in the potatoes and arrange them across the pan with space where possible; do not stir at first.
Once the bottom faces are browned, turn sections of potatoes and continue until several surfaces have colour.
Make a clear patch in the pan, melt in the butter, and add the onion and red pepper to that spot.
Cook the vegetables until they soften and pick up a little colour, then mix them through the potatoes.
Sprinkle over the paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper, and turn gently so the seasoning reaches every cube.
Give the mixture a final few minutes in the skillet, checking that the potato centres are tender before adding parsley and serving.
tips: Start with similarly sized cubes so they soften and brown at the same pace.
Letting the drained potatoes shed steam helps the oil brown them rather than trapping moisture.
Choose the widest skillet available so the potatoes have contact with the hot surface.
commonMistakes: Filling the pan too deeply leaves the potatoes soft because steam cannot escape.
Turning every minute interrupts the crust that gives home fries their colour.
Cooking the potatoes until fully soft in water makes them prone to breaking apart in the skillet.
substitutions: Yukon Gold potatoes make a richer, more buttery-tasting alternative to russets.
A green or yellow bell pepper can stand in for the red pepper.
Bacon drippings can replace avocado oil for a deeper savoury flavour.
storage: Refrigerate cooled home fries in a covered container for up to 4 days.
Reheat them in a lightly oiled hot skillet until the edges are crisp again.
They can be frozen for up to 1 month, although freshly cooked potatoes have the best contrast of textures.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Breakfast Tacos
description: Warm tortillas filled with softly cooked eggs, savoury chorizo, melting cheese, avocado, and bright pico de gallo for a flexible Tex-Mex breakfast.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese
Fresh cilantro and hot sauce, for serving
instructions: Set a skillet over medium heat and cook the chorizo, breaking it apart with a spoon, until no pink meat remains and the pieces are browned.
Spoon the chorizo onto a warm plate, leaving just enough rendered fat in the pan to flavour the next component if desired.
Heat the tortillas one at a time in a dry pan or briefly over a low flame until pliable with a few toasted spots.
Wrap the warmed tortillas in a clean towel or keep them covered so they stay flexible.
Beat the eggs, milk, and salt together until the yolks and whites are fully combined.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat, then add the egg mixture.
Draw a spatula slowly across the base of the pan as soft curds form; take the pan off the heat while they still look glossy.
Place eggs in the centre of each tortilla and scatter the cheese over them while both are warm.
Finish with chorizo, avocado, pico de gallo, cilantro, and as much hot sauce as suits the table.
Fold or serve open-faced straight away, before the tortillas cool and the eggs firm up.
tips: Keep tortillas covered after warming to prevent their edges from drying out.
Gentle heat gives the scrambled eggs a tender texture and leaves time to assemble the toppings.
Put toppings in small bowls so each person can adjust salsa, avocado, and hot sauce.
commonMistakes: High heat sets scrambled eggs too quickly and can make them rubbery.
Filling tortillas straight from the package makes them more likely to tear when folded.
Packing in too much filling can cause the taco to split and spill.
substitutions: Crisp bacon is a suitable swap when fresh chorizo is unavailable.
Use corn tortillas for a naturally gluten-free option, checking all packaged ingredients as needed.
Seasoned black beans can replace the meat for a vegetarian filling.
storage: Refrigerate cooled eggs and chorizo in separate covered containers for up to 3 days.
Warm eggs slowly in a skillet and heat tortillas separately before assembling.
Cut avocado and add pico de gallo only at serving time for the freshest texture.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
